$comment: Synthesized MPEG-TS samples for the player's demuxer regression tests. Not recordings: each is produced by the ffmpeg command in its entry, so `make fixtures-refresh` does not apply. Committed as base64 text (.b64) so a reviewer can diff them; a test decodes the text. Byte-identical regeneration needs the same x264 build (its version is embedded in the stream's SEI); what a test relies on is the shape the entry describes, not the bytes.

video-before-audio.mpegts.b64.source: ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=0x202020:s=64x36:r=12:d=2.4" -itsoffset 1.0 -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:d=1.4" -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -tune zerolatency -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 12 -x264-params "bframes=0:keyint=12:min-keyint=12:scenecut=0" -b:v 40k -c:a aac -b:a 24k -ac 1 -muxdelay 0 -muxpreload 0 -output_ts_offset 0.184 -f mpegts video-before-audio.mpegts (ffmpeg 7, x264 core 164 r3108), then base64 -w 76
video-before-audio.mpegts.b64.notes: One program: H.264 (Constrained Baseline, 64x36 @ 12 fps, IDR first) from 0.184 s, AAC-LC 48 kHz mono from 1.163 s, 2.42 s long. The provider's shape — video under one second, audio after it — that hls.js 1.6.16 misread as a 33-bit rollover, dropping the first segment's video. `encoding` says the file is base64 text, so `size` and `sha256` are of the decoded stream.
